```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Peters_2016_ilofotaseAlfa"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Peters_2016_ilofotaseAlfa"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-016-0399-y> (open access, PMC5021756)

Ilofotase alfa is the human recombinant alkaline phosphatase (recAP), a
chimeric enzyme built from the human intestinal alkaline phosphatase with the
crown domain of the placental isoenzyme. It was developed for sepsis-associated
acute kidney injury. Peters 2016 reports its first-in-human trial and the
population PK model used to choose the doses for the phase IIa/b STOP-AKI trial.

# Population

The model was fitted to serum recAP concentrations from 36 healthy adult
volunteers in a single-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled
phase I trial in the Netherlands (EudraCT 2013-002694-21). In part A, four
groups received a single 1-h IV infusion of 200, 500, 1000 or 2000 U/kg (six
PK-evaluable subjects per dose); in part B, two groups received 500 or
1000 U/kg as a 1-h infusion on three consecutive days (six per dose). One
subject in the 200 U/kg group was dosed short because the infusion set leaked
and was excluded from the PK analysis (Peters 2016 Table 1).

Eligibility was 18-55 years and BMI 18-30 kg/m^2. Across the active arms,
group-mean age was 21-33 years and group-mean weight 69.4-73.8 kg; 18 of the
37 actively dosed subjects were women and 35 were white (Table 2). The model
has no covariates: age, weight, sex, height, lean body mass and BMI were
screened on V1 and K10 and none improved the fit.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Peters_2016_ilofotaseAlfa")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lkel` (K10) | log(0.666) 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(3.71) L | Table 3 |
| `lk12`, `lk21` | log(0.311), log(0.0143) 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lk13`, `lk31` | log(0.545), log(0.571) 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lk14`, `lk41` | log(0.564), log(0.0795) 1/h | Table 3 |
| `etalkel` variance | 0.026893 | Table 3, IIV on K10 16.51% CV |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.078887 | Table 3, IIV on V1 28.65% CV |
| `etalkel`-`etalvc` covariance | -0.036100 | Back-solved from Table 3 IIV on CL 18.48% CV (see Assumptions) |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.02) | Table 3, residual error 0.02 |
| Four-compartment structure, IIV on V1 and K10 with covariance, proportional error | n/a | Results, Pharmacokinetic Modeling |
| %CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1) x 100 | n/a | Methods (formula image in the online version) |
| CL = K10 V1; Vx = K1x V1 / Kx1 (derived rows of Table 3) | n/a | Table 3; checked below |

Paper compartments 2, 3 and 4 map to `peripheral1`, `peripheral2` and
`peripheral3`.

# Dose conversion: U/kg to micrograms

The model works in mass: `central` holds micrograms, V1 is in litres and `Cc` is
in ng/mL (ug/L), the unit the electrochemiluminescence assay reported. The
trial dosed in activity units per kilogram of actual body weight, and Peters
2016 does not state the specific activity used to convert the dose to mass for
the fit.

The phase IIa/b trial for which these doses were chosen (STOP-AKI,
NCT02182440) gave the same three regimens, 250, 500 and 1000 U/kg, and its
report expresses them as 0.4, 0.8 and 1.6 mg/kg (Pickkers et al., JAMA
2018;320(19):1998-2009, PMID 30357272). That is 625 U/mg, which this vignette
uses. Figure 4 of Peters 2016 checks it independently below: the median curve
the authors simulated for 1000 U/kg implies 627-641 U/mg (see below).

The paper also equates its target of 290 U/L with 170 ng/mL (about 1700 U per
mg). That figure relates the serum AP activity measured by the clinical
chemistry analyser to recAP mass; it is not the dose unit. Using it to convert
the dose under-predicts every concentration in Figures 1, 3 and 4 by about
2.7-fold.

```{r dose-conversion}
u_per_mg <- 625
dose_ug <- function(dose_u_per_kg, wt) dose_u_per_kg * wt / u_per_mg * 1000
```

# Derived parameters

Table 3 prints CL, V2, V3 and V4 next to the estimated rate constants. These are
recomputed from the packaged values; agreement is to the rounding of the
printed rate constants.

```{r derived}
mod <- readModelDb("Peters_2016_ilofotaseAlfa")
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
th <- setNames(exp(ini_df$est), ini_df$name)
derived <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("CL (L/h)", "V2 (L)", "V3 (L)", "V4 (L)"),
  packaged = c(
    th[["lkel"]] * th[["lvc"]],
    th[["lk12"]] * th[["lvc"]] / th[["lk21"]],
    th[["lk13"]] * th[["lvc"]] / th[["lk31"]],
    th[["lk14"]] * th[["lvc"]] / th[["lk41"]]
  ),
  table3 = c(2.47, 80.5, 3.54, 26.3)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (packaged - table3) / table3)
knitr::kable(derived, digits = c(0, 3, 2, 2))
# K21 is printed to three significant figures (0.0143), which alone moves
# V2 by up to 0.35%.
stopifnot(all(abs(derived$pct_diff) < 1))
```

The back-solved covariance reproduces the IIV that Table 3 prints for CL and,
since only V1 carries an eta, the identical 28.65% it prints for V2, V3 and V4.

```{r derived-iiv}
om <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$omega
cv <- function(v) 100 * sqrt(exp(v) - 1)
iiv <- c(
  K10 = cv(om["etalkel", "etalkel"]),
  V1 = cv(om["etalvc", "etalvc"]),
  CL = cv(sum(om))
)
round(iiv, 2)
stopifnot(abs(iiv - c(16.51, 28.65, 18.48)) < 0.01)
```

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. Subjects are simulated with body weight drawn
from a normal distribution with the pooled mean and SD of the active arms in
Table 2, as the authors did for their dose-selection simulations. Weight
enters only through the U/kg dose.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2016)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)

tab2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n, ~mean, ~sd,
  7, 69.4, 10.6,
  6, 72.9, 9.0,
  6, 69.9, 16.3,
  6, 69.4, 8.2,
  6, 73.8, 13.0,
  6, 69.8, 14.8
)
wt_mean <- sum(tab2$n * tab2$mean) / sum(tab2$n)
wt_sd <- sqrt(
  (sum((tab2$n - 1) * tab2$sd^2) + sum(tab2$n * (tab2$mean - wt_mean)^2)) /
    (sum(tab2$n) - 1)
)
c(mean = wt_mean, sd = wt_sd)

sad_times <- c(
  0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.92, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48,
  72, 120, 192
)

make_cohort <- function(n, dose_u_per_kg, n_doses, obs_times, label,
                        id_offset = 0L) {
  wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, wt_mean, wt_sd), 45), 110)
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_times <- 24 * (seq_len(n_doses) - 1)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(
      WT = wt[id - id_offset],
      amt = dose_ug(dose_u_per_kg, WT),
      rate = amt, # 1-h infusion
      evid = 1L
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(WT = wt[id - id_offset], amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", treatment = label) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events_sad <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(200, 200, 1, sad_times, "200 U/kg", id_offset = 0L),
  make_cohort(200, 500, 1, sad_times, "500 U/kg", id_offset = 200L),
  make_cohort(200, 1000, 1, sad_times, "1000 U/kg", id_offset = 400L),
  make_cohort(200, 2000, 1, sad_times, "2000 U/kg", id_offset = 600L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_sad[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_sad <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_sad, keep = c("treatment", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(
    treatment,
    levels = c("200 U/kg", "500 U/kg", "1000 U/kg", "2000 U/kg")
  ))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1A: single ascending doses

```{r figure-1a, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim_sad |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 24) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(gm = exp(mean(log(Cc))), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, gm, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion (h)",
    y = "Serum recAP (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Single 1-h infusion, geometric mean of simulated subjects",
    caption = "Replicates the upper panel of Figure 1A of Peters 2016."
  )
```

Read approximately from the figure, Figure 1A peaks at about 1700, 6000,
12000 and 26000 ng/mL for 200, 500, 1000 and 2000 U/kg; the text gives the
range of mean peaks as 1715 to 26,253 ng/mL. The model is linear, so its peaks are dose-proportional; the
observed 200 U/kg peak is lower than proportional, and the model
over-predicts that group (see the NCA comparison below).

The text states that about 10% of the maximum concentration remains 4 h after
the start of the infusion and under 5% at 24 h. The typical subject reproduces
both:

```{r fraction-remaining}
typ_amt <- dose_ug(1000, 70)
typ_events <- rxode2::et(amt = typ_amt, rate = typ_amt, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(sad_times)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events) |>
  as.data.frame()
frac <- typ$Cc[typ$time %in% c(4, 24)] / max(typ$Cc)
names(frac) <- c("4 h", "24 h")
round(100 * frac, 1)
stopifnot(frac[["4 h"]] > 0.05, frac[["4 h"]] < 0.15, frac[["24 h"]] < 0.05)
```

## Figure 3: visual predictive check at 500 U/kg

The authors' VPC normalises every observation to 500 U/kg, once (left) or
once daily for three days (right).

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
vpc_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.25), seq(3, 200, by = 1))))
mad_times <- sort(unique(c(
  vpc_times[vpc_times <= 96],
  24 + seq(0, 2, by = 0.25), 48 + seq(0, 2, by = 0.25)
)))
events_vpc <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(200, 500, 1, vpc_times, "Single dose", id_offset = 0L),
  make_cohort(200, 500, 3, mad_times, "Once daily x 3", id_offset = 200L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_vpc[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_vpc, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_vpc |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("Single dose", "Once daily x 3"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Serum recAP (ng/mL)",
    title = "500 U/kg 1-h infusion: median and 95% prediction interval",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Peters 2016."
  )
```

In the published single-dose panel the median falls to about 12 ng/mL by 200 h;
in the multiple-dose panel the trough before the third dose is about 200 ng/mL.

## Figure 4: 1000 U/kg once daily for three days

Figure 4 is the authors' simulation of the high dose chosen for the patient
trial. The maintainers read the median curve at its peak and at four
later times from the published figure (log axis; about +/-10% reading
error).

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
fig4_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 150, by = 0.5), 1, 23.99, 25, 47.99, 49, 147)))
events_fig4 <- make_cohort(200, 1000, 3, fig4_times, "1000 U/kg x 3")
sim_fig4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_fig4) |>
  as.data.frame()
fig4_sum <- sim_fig4 |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fig4_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label, ~time, ~published,
  "End of first infusion", 1, 13500,
  "Trough before dose 2", 23.99, 290,
  "Trough before dose 3", 47.99, 450,
  "End of third infusion", 49, 14000,
  "147 h", 147, 170
)

ggplot(filter(fig4_sum, time > 0), aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 170, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = fig4_digitised, aes(time, published), colour = "red") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Serum recAP (ng/mL)",
    title = "1000 U/kg 1-h infusion once daily for 3 days",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Peters 2016. Red points: median read from the",
      "published figure. Dashed line: 170 ng/mL target trough."
    )
  )

fig4_cmp <- fig4_digitised |>
  left_join(fig4_sum |> select(time, med), by = "time") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (med - published) / published)
fig4_cmp |>
  rename(
    "Time point" = label, "Time (h)" = time,
    "Figure 4 median (ng/mL)" = published, "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = med,
    "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# A wrong dose conversion (the 290 U/L = 170 ng/mL equivalence) puts every
# point about 63% low, and a mis-transcribed V1 or K10 moves the peak or the
# troughs by tens of percent; reading error from the figure is about 10%.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(fig4_cmp$pct_diff)) < 15,
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$pct_diff) < 30)
)
```

The specific activity implied by Figure 4 alone, scaling the 625 U/mg
conversion by the simulated-to-published ratio at each point:

```{r implied-activity}
round(u_per_mg * fig4_cmp$med / fig4_cmp$published)
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA is run on the four single-dose groups at the trial's sampling times
(0-192 h after the start of the infusion).

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_sad |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time != 1) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- events_sad |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = levels(sim_sad$treatment))) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
  concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h"
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
  doseu = "ug", route = "intravascular", duration = 1
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against published values

The paper reports the mean peak concentrations of the lowest and highest doses
(1715 and 26,253 ng/mL; Results) and an apparent terminal half-life of 48 h
(Discussion, dose not stated, so it is compared with every group). Simulated
values are the medians over subjects.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~half.life,
  "200 U/kg", 1715, 48,
  "500 U/kg", NA, 48,
  "1000 U/kg", NA, 48,
  "2000 U/kg", 26253, 48
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published NCA. * differs from the published value by >20%.")
```

The 2000 U/kg peak agrees. The 200 U/kg peak is over-predicted by about half:
the observed peaks rise more than dose-proportionally between 200 and
2000 U/kg (1715 x 10 = 17,150 against 26,253 observed), and the published model
is linear, so it cannot match both ends.

The simulated NCA half-life over 0-192 h, about 66 h, is longer than the 48 h
the Discussion quotes. The packaged model's terminal phase is set mainly by
K21 = 0.0143 1/h, and the authors' own model-based VPC in Figure 3 shows the
same slow tail (about 25 ng/mL at 100 h and 12 ng/mL at 200 h after 500 U/kg,
read from the figure), a halving time of roughly 80-90 h. The 48 h figure is
the authors' NCA estimate from the observed profiles, not a model parameter,
so the difference is reported rather than adjusted.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dose units.** The paper does not give the specific activity used to put
  the U/kg doses into mass for the fit. The maintainers use 625 U/mg, from
  the STOP-AKI report's equivalence of 1000 U/kg and 1.6 mg/kg for the same
  regimens; Figure 4 of Peters 2016 independently implies 627-641 U/mg. The
  paper's 290 U/L = 170 ng/mL equivalence relates measured serum AP activity to
  mass and is not used for dosing.
- **IIV covariance.** The text says the final model estimated a covariance
  between the K10 and V1 etas, but Table 3 does not print it. Table 3 does
  print the IIV on the derived CL (18.48% CV), and its identical 28.65% for V1
  to V4 shows that the derived-parameter IIVs were computed from the omega
  matrix. With CL = K10 x V1, var(eta_CL) = var(eta_K10) + var(eta_V1) +
  2 cov, which gives cov = -0.036100 (correlation -0.78). This is used.
- **%CV convention.** The Methods give %CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1) x 100,
  so variances are log(1 + CV^2).
- **Residual error.** Table 3's last row, labelled omega^2 with the footnote
  "residual error", is read as the variance of the proportional error, so
  `propSd = sqrt(0.02)` (14.1%). The text says a proportional error model was
  selected.
- **Body weight** for simulation is drawn from a normal distribution with the
  pooled mean and SD of the active arms (Table 2), truncated to 45-110 kg.
- **Simulated peak.** The infusion ends at 1 h, a time the trial did not
  sample (0.92 and 1.25 h); the NCA uses the trial's sampling times only, so
  the simulated Cmax is taken at the nearest sampled time as in the study.
- No erratum or correction notice for Peters 2016 was found (checked
  2026-11-24).
